transliteration: asvāmyanumatād dāsād asataś ca janād rahaḥ | hīnamūlyam avelāyāṃ krīṇaṃs taddoṣabhāg bhavet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who purchases from a non-owner without permission, from a slave, or from an unqualified person in secrecy, or at a price lower than value during improper time—such a one becomes partaker of that defect.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from rightful ownership validated by consciousness alignment
Causation arises through misaligned transactional intent
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and integrity of exchange
Restoration logic requires dissolution of defective acquisition and reintegration with dharmic flow
Consciousness alignment demands transparency, rightful source recognition, and temporal harmony
executable_legal_axioms: IF transaction occurs without owner's explicit consent AND source lacks ownership capacity THEN transaction invalid AND acquirer assumes liability for defect restoration
IF purchase made secretly OR below fair value AND outside prescribed time THEN acquirer bears full completion obligation
IF item acquired carries prior defect traceable to improper transfer THEN acquirer must execute conscious reversal protocol
IF transaction breaches dharma-timeframe THEN restoration includes temporal realignment process
IF acquirer knowingly engages in defective transaction THEN mandatory participation in integrity-reintegration cycle
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, transactions lacking clear ownership validation must be reviewed under the lens of consciousness-aligned authority. The threshold of responsibility lies not merely in legal title but in alignment with the source-consciousness of the property. Secrecy, undervaluation, or untimely execution triggers automatic restorative jurisdiction, bypassing punitive frameworks.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies defective acquisition as rooted in misalignment with source-consciousness. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential distortion in ownership integrity, leading to proportional responsibility. The non-punitive reality rule upholds that suffering is not justice; correction and reintegration restore balance without inflicting harm.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Sole Source of Legal Authority. This ruling restores Dharma through consciousness-realized justice. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
